job_description:
Deloitte is seeking a Data Engineer II to support the design, development, and delivery of data solutions that enable analytics, reporting, and business decision-making. This role will focus on building scalable data pipelines, improving data quality, and supporting modern data platform capabilities across client and business needs. The ideal candidate brings technical experience in data engineering, strong problem-solving skills, and the ability to work across teams in a dynamic environment.

Work you'll do

As a Data Engineer II on the Data Engineering team, you will be responsible for...

• Design, build, test, and maintain scalable data pipelines and workflows for ingesting, transforming, and delivering structured and unstructured data
• Develop and optimize data models, integration patterns, and storage solutions to support analytics, reporting, and operational use cases
• Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders to define data requirements, troubleshoot issues, and implement data quality controls
• Partner directly with government stakeholders to clarify ambiguous business problems, identify root causes, and translate needs into practical, secure, user-centered solutions.
• Design, build, enhance, and maintain solutions across Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, and SharePoint.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

• Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
• Effective written and verbal communication skills
• Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
• Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
• Ability to lead projects or workstreams
• Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
• Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
• Ability to meet deadlines
• Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

You will join a team that designs and delivers data engineering solutions that help organizations modernize data platforms and enable analytics, automation, and business insight. The team works across the data lifecycle, including ingestion, transformation, storage, quality, and delivery of data products. Team members collaborate with engineers, analysts, and business stakeholders to build scalable, reliable, and secure solutions.

Qualifications

Required:

• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, or a quantitative field
• 2+ years of experience designing, building, and maintaining data pipelines and ETL/ELT workflows
• 2+ years of experience using SQL, Python, and PySpark for data ingestion, transformation, and automation
• 1+ years of experience monitoring data pipelines, troubleshooting issues, and supporting data quality and system reliability
• 1+ years of experience with Power Platform development proficiency across Power Apps, Power Automate, Power BI, and SharePoint
• Ability to travel 10%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.
• Must possess an active U.S. Secret security clearance and be able to maintain it for the duration of employment and assignment
• Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

• Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Data Science, or a quantitative field
• 1+ years of experience using Palantir Foundry, including Pipeline Builder and Ontology-based data modeling
• 1+ years of experience with data warehousing platforms such as Snowflake, Databricks, or Amazon Redshift
• 1+ years of experience with version control and continuous integration tools

Position Title: Data Scientist

Position Overview: We are seeking a Data Scientist to support reclassification efforts across federal job series. The incumbent will apply advanced data analysis, statistical modeling, and computational techniques to workforce data and position descriptions, ensuring alignment with classification standards and helping inform accurate, data-driven decisions.

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor’s degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Human Resources Analytics, or a related field (Master’s preferred).

• Strong proficiency in programming languages such as Python or R.

• Experience with natural language processing (NLP), machine learning, and data visualization.

• Knowledge of SQL and database management.

• Ability to interpret and present complex data clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Key Responsibilities:

• Collect, clean, and analyze large datasets related to position descriptions, job duties, and workforce information.

• Use statistical methods, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning techniques to identify trends, patterns, and commonalities across job roles.

• Conduct text analytics on position descriptions to map tasks, skills, and responsibilities to appropriate job series and grade levels.

• Collaborate with human resources professionals, subject matter experts, and leadership to validate data-driven findings.

• Develop dashboards, visualizations, and reports to communicate insights in a clear and actionable manner.

• Ensure consistency, accuracy, and compliance with federal classification policies and standards.

• Provide recommendations to leadership on job reclassification and series alignment based on data analysis.

• Stay current with emerging trends in workforce analytics, HR technology, and data science.

Desired Skills:

• Familiarity with federal job classification standards and Office of Personnel Management (OPM) guidance.

• Experience working with workforce or HR-related data.

• Knowledge of cloud computing environments and big data tools.

• Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.

Impact: This position plays a key role in ensuring federal positions are accurately classified, improving workforce alignment, and enabling data-driven decision-making to support organizational goals.

Position: Graph Data Scientist

Location: Remote, with occasional site visits to PRAC locations as required

Work Environment: Remote

Salary Range: $125,000 - $165,000 per year

Knowesis, Inc. is seeking an experienced Graph Data Scientist to support the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC) by developing and applying advanced graph-based analytic techniques to detect fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement across federal programs. The PRAC delivers data-driven oversight of pandemic relief and OBBBA Act funds and works closely with federal Offices of Inspectors General (OIGs) and federal law enforcement to ensure that covered funds are used appropriately and not subject to fraud or misuse.

The Graph Data Scientist will play a critical role within the PRAC Analytics Center, applying graph theory, network science, and machine learning to uncover hidden relationships, detect complex fraud schemes, and support investigative case development. This position will contribute to PRAC's advanced analytic support, investigative intelligence, and capability development efforts by building graph models, knowledge graphs, link analysis products, and graph-based fraud detection tools.

The PRAC analytic platform operates in a cloud-based environment using tools such as Azure Databricks, Microsoft SQL Server, Microsoft Power BI, and neo4j, along with other advanced technologies to analyze and visualize public, non-public, and commercially available data. The Graph Data Scientist will work within agile sprints and Integrated Project Teams (IPTs), collaborating with PRAC stakeholders, OIG partners, and law enforcement to deliver high-quality analytic outputs that support oversight, investigative support, and continuous capability enhancement. The role requires strong technical expertise, analytic rigor, and the ability to translate complex graph-based insights into clear, actionable intelligence for diverse stakeholders.

The Job Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following:
• Develop graph-based analytic rules and models to detect fraud, waste, abuse, and mismanagement across multi-agency and multi-program datasets.
• Apply advanced graph theory concepts-including network topology, centrality measures, community detection, and shortest-path algorithms-to identify hidden relationships and emerging fraud schemes.
• Use Neo4j (or similar graph databases) and fluently write Cypher queries to build, test, and optimize graph models and knowledge graphs supporting PRAC analytic use cases.
• Conduct exploratory data analysis and data profiling on public and non-public datasets to prepare graph structures and ensure high-quality ingestion.
• Apply clustering, classification, anomaly detection, and other machine learning techniques to graph-structured data to enhance fraud detection capabilities.
• Design, implement, and optimize graph data pipelines, schemas, and data models that support high-complexity networks and large-scale analytic environments.
• Document methodologies, graph models, code, and analytic outputs in accordance with PRAC data governance, EDM standards, and federal oversight requirements.
• Collaborate with PRAC stakeholders, OIG partners, and law enforcement to refine analytic approaches, validate graph-based findings, and support cross-program risk identification.
• Conduct graph-based investigative analysis using open-source, law enforcement, and third-party data to support lead generation and case development.
• Build link analysis diagrams, entity relationship charts, and graph-based intelligence products that visualize complex networks and relationships across multiple data sources.
• Use graph analytics to validate PRAC-developed analytic rules and model outputs, performing due diligence to confirm or refute potential fraud indicators.
• Support OIG and law enforcement partners by producing customized investigative work products and presenting graph-derived insights in clear, actionable formats.
• Follow PRAC investigative workflows, templates, and policies for handling law-enforcement-sensitive data and multi-agency investigative information.
• Evaluate emerging graph analytics tools, graph databases, and data sources; provide recommendations aligned with PRAC mission needs and federal policy.
• Collaborate with PRAC's OCIO, OCISO, and OCDO to configure, integrate, and optimize approved graph tools within the PRAC analytic environment.
• Support ingestion of new data sources into graph environments, including schema design, transformation logic, and quality control.
• Assist PRAC in analyzing cutting-edge graph-based AI/ML tools and technologies, providing technical documentation and risk considerations to support Government procurement decisions.
• Maintain awareness of evolving fraud schemes, graph analytic techniques, and cross-program risks to inform future capability development.
• Work closely with data scientists, investigators, statisticians, and engineers to integrate graph analytics into broader fraud detection and investigative workflows.
• Communicate complex graph-based findings to senior PRAC leadership, OIG partners, and non-technical stakeholders in clear, accessible terms.
• Ensure analytic integrity, reproducibility, and compliance across all graph-related workstreams.
• Contribute to continuous improvement of analytic processes, data quality, and graph-based fraud detection methodologies.

Required Qualifications:
• Three (3) or more years of hands-on experience using Neo4j or similar graph databases, including fluency in Cypher or comparable graph query languages.
• Deep understanding of graph theory and network science, including network topology, centrality measures, community detection, and shortest-path algorithms.
• Three (3) or more years of hands-on experience applying statistical and machine learning techniques-such as clustering, classifiers, and anomaly detection-to graph-structured data.
• Three (3) or more years of experience applying graph methods to fraud detection, knowledge graph development, and identification of hidden relationships.
• Experience designing, implementing, and optimizing graph data pipelines, graph data models, and schemas supporting high-complexity networks.
• Strong Python programming skills, including use of standard machine learning libraries (e.g., Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-Learn, NetworkX).
• Strong oral and written communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience supporting fraud analytics, investigative support, or program integrity efforts within federal oversight environments (e.g., OIGs, PRAC, CIGIE, law enforcement).
• Experience integrating multi-agency or multiprogram datasets into graph environments to detect cross-program risks and complex fraud schemes.
• Experience producing graph-based investigative work products such as link analysis diagrams, entity relationship charts, and network visualizations.
• Experience developing or deploying AI/ML models applied to graph data.
• Experience supporting enterprise data management (EDM), data governance, and federal data quality standards.
• Familiarity with PRAC AI governance policies, OMB memoranda (M-25-22, M-25-21, M-26-04), and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
• Advanced certifications in data science, graph analytics, or fraud examination (e.g., CFE, Neo4j Certified Professional).

Required Education: Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) in Data Science, Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related quantitative field.

Preferred Education: Master's degree (MS/MA) in Data Science, Analytics, Computer Science, Statistics, or a related discipline.

Benefits:
• Health (PPO & HDHP) Insurance, Dental, Vision, STD & LTD, Basic Life Insurance, 401k Company Match, & Voluntary Products.

About Peregrine
Peregrine Advisors is a rapidly growing AI and data innovation hub helping government solve hard problems and deliver better outcomes. We work across the full lifecycle—from strategy and governance through architecture, engineering, analytics, AI, visualization, and training—for clients including the SEC, PCAOB, DDOT, and DCAA.

Our clients describe our support as “absolutely excellent” and our people as “instrumental to organization’s success.” Winner of the United Nations COP27 Datathon, our work has earned all Exceptional CPARS ratings, SEC Chair’s Awards, the SEC Vision Award, and recognition from FDA leadership.

We are also built differently. Peregrine is the first and only social enterprise organized as a Benefit Corporation and SBA 8(a) company focused on AI and data for government. We believe business success should create client value, social value, and opportunity for our people.

As we enter our next stage of growth, we need dependable, motivated, and skilled people who have a combination of intellectual curiosity and intellectual courage. With new clients, larger programs, and expanding responsibilities, the people joining Peregrine now will have the opportunity to help shape the company we become.
People first. Ownership always.
We solve problems through people, process, and technology—in that order. Technology matters, but people make transformation happen. That principle defines our culture. Trust and motivation are the foundational pillars of delivery on which our skills stand. We hire people we can trust, who care deeply about what they do, take ownership, learn quickly, help one another, and refuse to walk past a problem because it belongs to someone else.

At Peregrine, you are not joining simply to fill a position. You are joining a team, taking ownership of a mission, and helping build a company. If that excites you, we should talk.

At Peregrine Advisors, you will carry analytical questions for a federal agency from the data to a defensible, documented answer. But we hire people, not seats. As the work evolves, you will move to where the hardest problems are.

This is a remote position, although a hybrid arrangement based in the Washington, DC metropolitan area with openness to a variable commuting cadence is preferred. Wherever you work from, occasional travel to DC is part of the job. The initial engagement requires United States citizenship and the ability to obtain a Public Trust determination.
Your first project
Your first project will likely have you transforming client data, structured, semi-structured, and unstructured, into analytic processes and outcomes that help drive mission-critical initiatives. Depending on the assignment, you may:

• Frame analytical questions with the people who own the mission, and turn them into designs that can actually be tested.

• Build analyses and models in Python and Structured Query Language (SQL) on cloud-native data platforms hosted in Amazon Web Services (AWS).

• Build models that earn their place: forecasting, classification, risk scoring, and anomaly detection matched to the question, the data, and the scrutiny a federal decision has to survive.

• Design the evaluation that shows a model is fit for a client environment, with baselines, validation designs, error analysis, documented limits, and documentation that lets someone else verify your results.

• Build analytical features and datasets from large, messy, document-heavy corpora, including text extracted with Amazon Textract and analyzed with foundation models through Amazon Bedrock.

• Harden one-off notebooks into repeatable, reviewed analytical pipelines.

• Put findings in front of decision-makers in plain language, with visuals that carry the argument instead of decorating it.

• Use artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted analysis as standard practice, with language models and coding assistants across the lifecycle and your judgment on top.

Adaptability and a demonstrated capacity to learn new concepts, systems, and tools are what keep you ahead of program needs as projects complete and priorities shift.
Who you are
You are rigorous about method and honest about uncertainty: when the evidence supports a narrower claim, you make the narrower claim. You care what the data is for, not just what it contains, and you would rather spend a day understanding the process that produced a number than a week modeling it wrong. You experiment, fail, learn, and repeat quickly. You would rather own an outcome than be handed a task.
What you bring

• A working command of statistics and machine learning applied to real operational data, not just curated coursework sets.

• The engineering habits that make analysis trustworthy: version control, reproducible pipelines, tested transformations, and documentation someone else can follow.

• The communication craft to make a technical result understandable to the people who depend on it.

• The precision to work where accuracy and auditability are not optional.

When we talk
Be prepared to discuss a difficult problem you worked through, the decisions you made, what happened, and what you learned.
What we offer
You will work alongside developers, engineers, data scientists, architects, and strategists, on work ranging from strategy to implementation. We support your development across assignments and clients through extensive onboarding, sponsored professional certifications such as the Data Management Capability Assessment Model (DCAM) and AWS technical certifications, and rotation across functions to expand your skills and perspective. The mission is real, the problems are hard, and you own what you ship.
What we commit to
As a Benefit Corporation, our commitment runs three ways: real, measurable value for our clients; government that works better for the public; and a team that makes everyone in it better.

We hire people who want to help build the firm, not just work at it. If that is you, apply.

job_title: Principal Data Scientist - AI for Data and Assessment
job_description:
Principal Data Scientist - AI for Data and Assessment

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Fast-forward a few years, and this little innovation and our passion for data has skyrocketed us to a Fortune 200 company and a leader in the world of data-driven decision-making.

As a Data Scientist at Capital One, you’ll be part of a team that’s leading the next wave of disruption at a whole new scale, using the latest in computing and machine learning technologies and operating across billions of customer records to unlock the big opportunities that help everyday people save money, time and agony in their financial lives.

Team Description

The AI for Data team builds and ships state of the art machine learning solutions to support data lifecycle within the enterprise. We partner with product, tech and design teams to deliver personalized experiences to our data and platform users to drive productivity and innovation. You will be the driving force to experiment, innovate and create next generation experiences powered by the latest emerging ML technologies.

In this role, you will:
• Partner with a cross-functional team of data scientists, software engineers, and product managers to deliver a product customers love
• Leverage a broad stack of technologies — Python, Conda, AWS, H2O, Spark, and more — to reveal the insights hidden within huge volumes of numeric and textual data
• Build machine learning models through all phases of development, from design through training, evaluation, validation, and implementation
• Flex your interpersonal skills to translate the complexity of your work into tangible business goals

The Ideal Candidate is:
• Innovative. You continually research and evaluate emerging technologies. You stay current on published state-of-the-art methods, technologies, and applications and seek out opportunities to apply them.
• Creative. You thrive on bringing definition to big, undefined problems. You love asking questions and pushing hard to find answers. You’re not afraid to share a new idea.
• Technical. You’re comfortable with open-source languages and are passionate about developing further. You have hands-on experience developing data science solutions using open-source tools and cloud computing platforms.
• Statistically-minded. You’ve built models, validated them, and back tested them. You know how to interpret a confusion matrix or a ROC curve. You have experience with clustering, classification, sentiment analysis, time series, and deep learning.
• A data guru. "Big data" doesn't faze you. You have the skills to retrieve, combine, and analyze data from a variety of sources and structures. You know understanding the data is often the key to great data science.

Basic Qualifications:
• Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining one of the following with an expectation that the required degree will be obtained on or before the scheduled start date:
• A Bachelor's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) plus 5 years of experience performing data analytics
• A Master's Degree in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field) or an MBA with a quantitative concentration plus 3 years of experience performing data analytics
• A PhD in a quantitative field (Statistics, Economics, Operations Research, Analytics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field)

Preferred Qualifications:
• Master’s Degree in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics) plus 3 years of experience in data analytics, or PhD in “STEM” field (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics)
• At least 1 year of experience working with AWS
• At least 3 years’ experience in Python, SQL
• At least 3 years’ experience with Deep Learning Frameworks
• At least 3 years’ experience with Natural Language Processing
